# Scientific review

**Correctness — PASS.** The ten nodes are explicitly parameterized. Their ideal is generated by five quadrics; two exact reduced Gröbner bases provide standard-monomial staircases of lengths ten and fifty and show that the coordinate \(x_0\) is a nonzerodivisor in both quotients. Together with the independent doubled-point length of fifty, this proves the *unsaturated* ideal equality \(I^{(2)}=I^2+(F)\). Normal-form calculations determine the exact defect pairing, verify that every cubic in the maximal homogeneous ideal annihilates its generator, and establish the Gorenstein Hilbert vector. Reproducibility checks are not substitutes for the stated rank and saturation proof.

**Originality — PASS, qualified.** Dolgachev's full accessible discussion of the Segre cubic provides the ten-node geometry, and Bocci–Harbourne's full accessible paper gives general symbolic-power/containment theory for point sets (mostly in the plane); neither inspected text presents the exact unsaturated squared-node ideal or the Gorenstein \((1,5,1)\) defect of these ten points. Relevant searches also compared aliases such as doubled Segre nodes, fat points, saturation, and Hilbert series. No direct coverage was found in the accessible indexed mathematical records. H. F. Baker's 1936 paper on polarities of these nodes was only abstract-accessible, so historical priority remains uncertain. Absence from search results is not a proof of global novelty.

**Mathematical value — PASS.** This is the uniquely extremal ten-node cubic threefold, so its complete doubled-node interpolation system is intrinsic rather than an arbitrary point experiment. The defect has a nontrivial structured Gorenstein duality, identifying exactly how the ordinary square fails to impose all order-two conditions. The Hilbert series and minimal generators also give a complete, reusable interpolation calculation in \(\mathbb P^4\), not just an isolated point count.

**Limitations and risks.** Characteristic zero, the second symbolic power only, and this fixed Segre node configuration. Older literature may have stated an equivalent calculation under polarization or apolarity terminology. No independent scientific audit has been conducted.

Self-review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
